Appearance:
 Shri Om Prakash Mathur - Advocate for the appellants
 Shri Rajesh Gupta- Advocate for respondent No.3/Insu
 Company.

Shri Anshuman Dudawat, learned counsel for the respo  No.2/Owner.
 ORDER

This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 , being aggrieved by the Award dated 02.12.2015 passed by the Second Additional, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Shivpuri (M.P.) (in short "the Claims Tribunal" ) in Claim Case No.17/2014.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appeal seeks enhancement of compensation on the ground of inadequacy.
2. The date of accident, issue of negligence and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28051 2 MA-257-2016 3.

As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Leelavati Kevat in the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.85,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the Award passed by the Claims Tribunal is contrary to the settled principles of law and suffers from serious errors of appreciation of evidence.

It is further submitted that in the motor accident, the parents (mother and father) of the claimants had died, and the appellants had preferred two claim petitions before the Claims Tribunal, one for compensation in respect of the death of their father, Motilal, in Claim Case No. 18/2014, and another in respect of the death of their mother, Leelavati, in Claim Case No. 17/2014.

However, the Tribunal awarded compensation in Claim Case No. 18/2014 for the death of their father, but erroneously assessed compensation to the tune of only Rs. 85,000/- in respect of the death of their mother, by recording a finding that the appellants/claimants were not dependent upon their mother.
Such a finding is erroneous and the amount awarded is on the lower side, warranting enhancement.

It is further contended that the Claims Tribunal committed error in not awarding reasonable compensation under the head of loss of consortium, in not applying an appropriate multiplier, in failing to add the component of future prospects, and in not granting just and reasonable amounts under other conventional heads, such as loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Hence, it is prayed that a reasonable and just amount of compensation be awarded to the claimants by enhancing the impugned NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28051 3 MA-257-2016 Award.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent Nos.2 and 3 contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.

6. Heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and perused the impugned Award.
7.
On perusal of the record, it is found that in the motor accident, the parents of the claimants had died.
The Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation only on the ground of loss of dependency in Claim Case No. 18/2014, in regard to the death of their father.
The finding of the Claims Tribunal that the appellants were not dependent on their mother is not just and proper.
The claimants, being the children of the deceased parents, were equally dependent on both their mother and father.
The work of a housewife cannot be undervalued or assessed on a lower scale while determining compensation.
A housewife is the manager of her household, and the services rendered by her cannot be measured merely in monetary terms.
The role of a housewife in managing and maintaining the household is invaluable, and therefore, it would not be appropriate to hold that the children were not dependent upon their mother.
While determining the compensation, the income of a woman engaged in household work should be assessed in accordance with the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act.
It is undisputed that the accident occurred on 20.11.2013.
At that time, the income of an unskilled worker, as per the Minimum Wages Act, was Rs. 5,520/- per month.

Accordingly, this Court deems it appropriate to assess the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:28051 4 MA-257-2016 income of deceased Leelavati at Rs. 5,520/- per month for the purpose of calculating the compensation.

8. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects of 25%.

9. Accordingly, appellants- claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD A  Income Rs.5520 X 12=
 Future Prospects25% Rs.82,800/-
 Dependency 2/3 Rs.55,200/-
 Multiplier 14 Rs.7,72,800/-
 Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 3  Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
 Total Compensatio 10.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.9,22,800/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.85,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.8,37,800/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28051 5 MA-257-2016 11.
In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.8,37,800/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
13. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of.
